course_name_original: SISTEMI ENERGETICI PER L'AMBIENTE, AD IDROGENO E PER P2G M (99540)
course_name_en: ENERGY SYSTEMS FOR THE ENVIRONMENT, HYDROGEN AND P2G M

learning_outcomes.text: Provide student with knowledge on design and operational issues of modern energy systems with reference to their impact on the environment, mainly in terms of pollutants formation and the advanced solutions for emissions removal.
Acquire knowledge on hydrogen-powered systems and machines for the environment, required for the implementation of power-to-gas energy conversion strategies.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and atmospheric pollution from energy systems
Combustion fundamentals for environmental impact analysis
Environmental impact of gas turbine units and combined cycles
Use of hydrogen in energy systems and gas turbines
Exercise on numerical tools for combustion simulation
Thermal pollution and cooling systems for energy systems
ORC systems, sCO2 systems and waste heat recovery
Environmental impact of advanced external-combustion systems
Non-combustion renewable energy systems and hybrid systems
teaching_methods: Visit to the energy systems laboratory (optional)
assessment_rules: Assessment is expressed on a scale of 30. To pass, students must demonstrate mastery of key concepts and ability to use technical language. Higher marks are for full understanding and appropriate use of content. Failure results from insufficient fundamental knowledge or limited command of technical language. If part of an integrated course, the final mark is the arithmetic mean, rounded up, of the marks obtained in the modules. 30 cum laude is awarded if 30 is obtained in both modules and cum laude in at least one.
bibliography: Lecture notes and slides available after each lesson.
